subject.title: Enhancement: Developer experience quick wins from code analysis

question: Where, if anywhere, should OpenClaw expose that an explicit skill command was routed through the model rather than dispatched directly to a tool?
rationale: The remaining change concerns the visibility and severity of expected routing behavior; source inspection cannot decide whether operators should see it routinely, only during debugging, or not at all.

options.title: Structured debug signal
options.body: Emit a trace or debug event for model-routed skill commands without presenting expected behavior as a warning.

options.title: Always-visible warning
options.body: Log a warning for every model-routed skill invocation, maximizing visibility at the cost of routine noise.

options.title: Keep documentation only
options.body: Treat the documented model-versus-tool dispatch distinction as sufficient and close the remaining request.

recommendation.title: Structured debug signal
recommendation.body: Emit a trace or debug event for model-routed skill commands without presenting expected behavior as a warning.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior maintainer-context review retained this exact routing-observability decision, and relevant history connects this person to the skills and command-routing surfaces.
